scope: Append-only revalidation of the two remaining Farris Great Land Register provinces that have not yet been admitted to the EU5 lower-bound set. Awaji is now mappable through the explicit EU5 location tag; Wakasa remains a useful documentary floor but has no verified EU5 province selector.

promotion_audit.decision: Promote Awaji as a conservative one-sided local-food lower bound. Retain Wakasa as validation-only because the EU5 geometry inventory has no distinct Wakasa selector. Neither record is a two-sided capacity anchor or an independent scale family.
promotion_audit.review_method: Re-read Farris (2006) Table 1.3 and surrounding methodology, including the register dates, rice-acreage conversion, omitted non-rice sensitivity and famine/shortage discussion. Checked current EU5 geometry tags rather than assuming the older review's selector inventory.
promotion_audit.reason_awaji_is_lower_bound_only: Farris's unbracketed 1280 value is a rice-supported minimum derived from registered acreage. The bracketed value adds an assumed 40 percent non-rice population and is not an uncertainty interval. No saturation fraction or upper endpoint is inferred.
required_followup: Keep Awaji grouped with the other Farris provinces in source-family holdouts; it is not independent evidence for global scale.
Add a historically matched Wakasa EU5 province or location polygon before using the Wakasa floor quantitatively.
Do not promote any Great Land Register value to a two-sided target without non-rice, fisheries, trade and upper-pressure evidence.

records.label: Awaji province, Kamakura Great Land Register local-food population floor
records.interval_semantics: Farris (2006) Table 1.3 gives an unbracketed 14,631-person 1280 value from Awaji's registered rice acreage using 0.181 chō per adult and a 16 percent child allowance. This is a conservative local rice-supported floor, not a complete population estimate or an intrinsic capacity ceiling. The bracketed 20,483 value assumes an additional 40 percent non-rice population and is excluded from the label.
pressure_evidence: Farris (2006), Table 1.3 and pp. 22-26, documents Awaji's Great Land Register and the rice-acreage-to-person conversion used for the 1280 estimate.

Farris (2006), pp. 29-32, frames late Kamakura demographic constraints through food supply, grain shortages and recurrent famine; the lower endpoint therefore represents food that registered local rice land could support, not a comfortable surplus.

The 1287 Awaji estate complaint records excessive demands on laborers and packhorses and seizure of wheat harvests and paddy/dry fields, a local pressure and extraction signal independent of the EU5 starting population.
Awaji is a bounded island province with wet rice, dry fields, fisheries and forest foods; omitted non-rice production is intentionally not filled into the floor.
shock_flags: Great Land Register is dated 1223; Farris labels the converted comparison year circa 1280
partial historical register and omitted non-rice fields
1287 estate extraction and farmer flight are pressure evidence, not a capacity endpoint
no independent saturation fraction or upper bound
records.trade_dependence: low_to_mixed; island rice and dry-field production with coastal exchange, but imports are not counted in the floor
records.food_regime: wet rice, dry fields, pulses, livestock, forest foods and Inland Sea fisheries
records.boundary_description: Medieval Awaji province (Awaji no kuni), represented by the current EU5 location tag awaji; the historical province is bounded but the selector is a geometry crosswalk, not a claim that all medieval cadastral edges are exact.
records.boundary_source: Harvard CHGIS Japan Historical GIS, Tokugawa Japan GIS 2004, jp_toku_kuni_pgn.shp, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0
records.source_family_independence: Same Farris Great Land Register source family as the existing Japan province floors; Awaji expands mapped coverage but is not an independent scale replication.
citation_details: Farris, Japan's Medieval Population (2006), Table 1.3, printed pp. 22-24 / PDF p. 34: Awaji 1280 rice-based value 14,631; bracketed non-rice sensitivity 20,483 is not used.
Farris (2006), Table 1.1, printed p. 14 / PDF p. 24: Awaji Great Land Register dated 1223, marked complete.
Farris (2006), pp. 29-32 / PDF pp. 39-42: rice acreage conversion, food supply, grain shortages and famine constraints.
Farris (2006), pp. 118-119 / PDF pp. 128-129, and note 57: 1287 Awaji estate abuse, wheat/paddy seizure and farmer flight.
records.notes: The current EU5 data contain an explicit awaji location tag, resolving the older review's mapping blocker. The floor remains conservative and source-family grouped; it cannot set global scale.

records.label: Wakasa province, Kamakura Great Land Register documentary floor
records.interval_semantics: Farris (2006) Table 1.3 gives a rice-based 14,215-person 1280 value from Wakasa's 1265 register. It is retained as a documentary local-food floor only; the bracketed 19,901 non-rice sensitivity, any saturation fraction and any capacity ceiling are excluded.
pressure_evidence: Farris (2006), Table 1.1, records the 1265 Wakasa Great Land Register and its 2,218 chō rice acreage; Table 1.3 applies the documented rice conversion to 14,215 people.
Farris (2006), pp. 14-17, compares the Wakasa register to Tara Estate surveys in 1254 and 1256, supporting the physical reality of the registered local paddy base.
The 1287 Tara Estate complaint records a land steward taking rice and dry-field crops and farmers absconding, showing extraction and food pressure without claiming saturation.
The Japan Sea coastal food system included dry fields, fisheries and forest foods omitted from the rice-only floor rather than statistically filled.
shock_flags: 1265 register is converted to the circa-1280 comparison year
EU5 has no distinct verified Wakasa province selector
partial non-rice coverage and no saturation fraction
1287 estate abuse and farmer flight are local pressure evidence
records.trade_dependence: low_to_mixed; local rice and coastal foods with regional exchange, but imports are not counted
records.food_regime: wet rice, dry fields, pulses, livestock, forest foods and Japan Sea fisheries
records.boundary_description: Medieval Wakasa province (Wakasa no kuni); the historical boundary is documented, but no distinct EU5 wakasa location/province selector is currently verified.
records.boundary_source: Harvard CHGIS Japan Historical GIS, Tokugawa Japan GIS 2004, jp_toku_kuni_pgn.shp, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0
records.source_family_independence: Same Farris Great Land Register source family as all Japan province floors; retained to prevent the known 14,215 value from being silently lost while its EU5 mapping is unresolved.
citation_details: Farris (2006), Table 1.3, printed pp. 22-24 / PDF p. 34: Wakasa 1280 rice-based value 14,215; bracketed non-rice sensitivity 19,901 is not used.
Farris (2006), Table 1.1, printed p. 14 / PDF p. 24: Wakasa Great Land Register dated 1265, marked complete.
Farris (2006), pp. 14-17 / PDF pp. 24-27: Tara Estate surveys provide an independent acreage check for the registered paddy base.
Farris (2006), pp. 118-119 / PDF pp. 128-129, and note 56: 1287 Tara Estate abuse, crop seizure and farmer flight.
records.notes: Validation-only until a Wakasa EU5 geometry selector is added and audited. Do not substitute all Echizen or another province.
